thread:
Sam Li: Quick heads-up — I repro'd a perf regression hitting paged-attn when the kernel selector falls back to the flashv2-compatible path for mid-length sequences. Microbench attached below.

Sam Li: microbench (seq=1024..2048, bs=8, warm):
```
baseline (flashv3 sticky): p50=28ms p95=42ms p99=58ms tokens/s=1450
with on-demand-slab + selector-fallback: p50=31ms p95=51ms p99=66ms tokens/s=1280
regression ~12% token throughput, p99 shifted +8ms
```

Maria V: ugh. did the kernel flip happen because of sequence-length bucketing or because of mem pressure?

Sam Li: Looks like both. Selector chooses flashv3 for long runs but when kv page cache triggers an on-demand slab alloc it forces a synchronous copy and we fall back to cpu-prefetch-friendly kernel for a few steps. The fallback then sticky-marks that stream and we oscillate.

Cheng Hu: @Sam can you paste a minimal trace from the runtime profiler? especially kernel-choice events + allocator ops. This smells like freelist exhaustion -> blocking path.

Sam Li: trace snippet:
```
[perf] t=0.102s kernel_select: flashv3
[alloc] t=0.103s slab_on_demand alloc page_id=0x7fa... size=2MB (sync copy)
[kernel] t=0.104s kernel_select: flashv2_fallback (latency bump)
[cache] t=0.110s kv_page_ready -> resume flashv3 
```

Olivia K: two quick ideas: 1) prefetch next kv page on hot prefix so alloc happens async before kernel-switch window. 2) change batching heuristic so we avoid mixing odd/even seq lengths in same microbatch which causes selector thrash.

Maria V: +1 on microbatching by length. We saw sticky kernel wins when batches are homogeneous. Could the allocator be doing too-small slab sizes causing fragmentation?

Cheng Hu: I suspect the slab granularity + on-demand policy leaves too many tiny fragments and the freelist get scanned on every alloc. Suggest trying: lockless freelist + slab-size bump heuristic (if page hot and request seq>1024, pre-allocate 4x page).

Sam Li: Tried Olivia's prefetch patch (branch: sam/prefetch-kv) — bench below. It reduced p99 by ~6ms but increased resident GPU memory and introduced occasional OOM on very small hosts.
```
sam/prefetch-kv: p50=29ms p95=45ms p99=60ms tokens/s=1370
```

Maria V: tradeoff is expected. We need a hybrid: prefetch only on sticky-hot keys and only if mem headroom>20%. Otherwise fall back to lightweight alloc.

Cheng Hu: I'll prototype lockless freelist + slab bump. Can someone run a systematic sweep across seq lengths and batch sizes? @bench-bot can you run: `bench/paged-attn --sweep "seq:256,512,1024,2048" --batch:4,8,16 --alloc:slab,on-demand,slab+prefetch` and paste summary?

bench-bot: Running sweep (job id 173820-sweep-3). ETA ~18m. Will post condensed numbers when done. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

(18m later)

bench-bot: Results (condensed):
```
alloc=on-demand: avg tokens/s drop 10-15% at seq>=1024, p99 up +10ms
alloc=slab: stable perf but higher mem (~+25%)
alloc=slab+prefetch: best p50/p95; p99 intermediate; mem highest
microbatching by seq length reduces kernel-flip events by ~85%
```

Olivia K: Nice. So immediate low-risk mitigation: change batcher to prefer same-length groups + raise slab bump threshold for seq>1024. Longer-term: freelist rewrite.

Sam Li: I'll open a small PR that: 1) groups microbatches by length, 2) increases slab bump threshold, 3) adds an opt-in prefetch flag gated by mem headroom.

Cheng Hu: I'll start a branch for the freelist rewrite and run unit perf. If we can make freelist non-blocking we may remove the need for prefetch in many cases.

Maria V: Also add trace hooks to count kernel-switch events per-stream so we can alert when selector oscillation > X/min.

Sam Li: Agreed. Thanks all. Filing follow-ups: #1 PR (sam) #2 freelist (cheng) #3 telemetry alert (maria).

Olivia K: :thumbsup:

bench-bot: linked artifacts: https://benchdash.internal/runs/173820-sweep-3 (summary + flamegraphs)

Sam Li: I'll paste a minimal repro script in the PR. If anyone wants to try earlier, run: `./tools/run_microbench --case=paged_attn --seq=2048 --bs=8 --alloc=on-demand`

Maria V: tagging this for the runtime perf retro next week.

Cheng Hu: cc @OliviaK for kernel selection heuristics design doc follow-up"
